vignettes.core_claim: Herbal treatment X is effective for chronic headaches.

auxiliaries.text: Most clinical trials of herbal treatment X underestimate its real benefits because they use the wrong dosing schedules or insensitive outcome measures.
Herbal treatment X mainly works for people with particular stress, sleep, or lifestyle profiles, so average trial results can hide genuine benefits.

core_evidence_disconfirming.text: A large preregistered randomized controlled trial with 800 participants found that herbal treatment X performed no better than placebo on validated headache outcomes.
A meta-analysis of 12 controlled studies found little consistent evidence that herbal treatment X improves chronic headaches more than placebo or usual care.

core_evidence_supporting.text: A small uncontrolled clinic report found that some patients taking herbal treatment X said their headaches improved over several weeks.

core_evidence_ambiguous.text: An online discussion thread includes several anecdotal reports that herbal treatment X helped headaches, but there is no verification, control group, or information on other treatments used.

auxiliary_evidence.text: A methodological review notes that some early herbal-treatment studies used inconsistent dosing and outcome measures, but later high-quality trials addressed many of these issues.
A secondary analysis suggests that stress level and sleep quality may influence headache outcomes, but evidence that they specifically change the effect of herbal treatment X is limited.

vignettes.core_claim: Vaccine Y causes long-term infertility in women.

auxiliaries.text: Studies claiming vaccine Y is safe use follow-up periods that are too short or too insensitive to detect real fertility problems.
Any fertility effect of vaccine Y may only appear in subgroups with specific hormonal, immune, or reproductive histories, so broad population studies can miss it.

core_evidence_disconfirming.text: A multi-country cohort study following 50,000 vaccinated and 50,000 unvaccinated women over five years found no difference in fertility rates, miscarriage rates, or birth outcomes between the groups.
A pooled review of fertility-related vaccine studies found that most well-powered analyses show no increased long-term infertility risk after vaccination.

core_evidence_supporting.text: A small fertility clinic reported that several patients who struggled to conceive had previously received vaccine Y, but it did not compare them to an unvaccinated group.

core_evidence_ambiguous.text: A viral video features several individuals who say they have not been able to conceive since getting vaccine Y, but it provides no medical records or information about other possible causes.

auxiliary_evidence.text: An independent review found that several fertility-related vaccine studies now include extended follow-up and clinically relevant reproductive outcomes rather than only short-term measures.
Some subgroup analyses have explored hormonal and reproductive-history differences, but they have not identified a reliable subgroup in which vaccine Y is linked to infertility.

vignettes.core_claim: The Z-diet is uniquely effective for long-term weight loss compared to standard calorie restriction.

auxiliaries.text: Studies that fail to find benefits for the Z-diet often include participants who do not follow the diet properly, making the diet look less effective than it is.
The Z-diet may work best when combined with particular exercise, sleep, or meal-timing patterns, so generic comparisons can miss its real advantage.

core_evidence_disconfirming.text: A meta-analysis of 15 randomized trials comparing the Z-diet to standard calorie restriction found no meaningful difference in average weight loss after two years.
A large comparative trial found that people assigned to the Z-diet lost about the same amount of weight as those on a standard calorie-restriction programme after one year.

core_evidence_supporting.text: A popular wellness clinic reported that many of its Z-diet clients lost substantial weight, but the report did not include a comparison group or long-term follow-up.

core_evidence_ambiguous.text: A best-selling Z-diet influencer shares dramatic before-and-after photos from followers, without specifying starting weights, adherence, or other lifestyle changes.

auxiliary_evidence.text: Reports from the largest Z-diet trials show generally good adherence monitoring, though not all studies verified diet compliance equally closely.
Some secondary analyses suggest sleep and exercise may influence overall weight loss, but evidence that they uniquely unlock the effect of the Z-diet is limited.

vignettes.core_claim: Commercial detox products are necessary to remove harmful toxins from the body.

auxiliaries.text: Standard medical tests cannot detect the subtle toxin build-up that detox products are supposed to remove.
Detox products may only help people with particular diets, exposures, or digestive profiles, so average trial results can hide real effects.

core_evidence_disconfirming.text: A clinical trial comparing several popular detox products to placebo found no differences in standard liver and kidney function tests or toxin-related blood markers after four weeks.
A review of detox-product studies concluded that there is no convincing evidence that these products remove toxins better than normal bodily processes.

core_evidence_supporting.text: A wellness centre reported that many clients said they felt more energised after using detox products, but there were no objective toxin measures or comparison group.

core_evidence_ambiguous.text: Online customer reviews include many reports of feeling cleaner or lighter after detox products, but provide no objective measurements and no information on other changes in diet or routine.

auxiliary_evidence.text: A professional body of clinical toxicologists states that current laboratory methods are sensitive enough to detect clinically relevant toxin accumulation in the body.
Some studies suggest that diet and environmental exposure influence toxin-related biomarkers, but there is little evidence that detox products specifically change outcomes in those subgroups.

vignettes.core_claim: Daily mindfulness practice can cure severe depression without medication or therapy.

auxiliaries.text: Clinical trials underestimate mindfulness because they do not allow enough time or enough intensity of practice for its full effects to appear.
Mindfulness may be sufficient for severe depression only in people with particular symptom profiles or life circumstances, so average treatment studies can miss those cases.

core_evidence_disconfirming.text: A meta-analysis of randomized trials found that mindfulness-based interventions can help but do not replace medication or structured therapy for severe depression, and combined treatment produces the best outcomes.
Long-term follow-up studies show that many people with severe depression who practise mindfulness still require therapy, medication, or both over time.

core_evidence_supporting.text: A meditation teacher reported that several students with severe depression improved dramatically using mindfulness alone, but no clinical assessment or comparison group was provided.

core_evidence_ambiguous.text: A blog post features one person who says mindfulness alone saved their life from severe depression, without discussing prior treatment, diagnosis, or other support.

auxiliary_evidence.text: Some mindfulness studies vary substantially in duration and intensity, but longer programmes still do not reliably show that mindfulness alone cures severe depression.
Researchers have explored whether severity profile or life context affects response to mindfulness, but there is little evidence that such factors make formal treatment unnecessary for severe cases.

vignettes.core_claim: The recent national election was rigged.

auxiliaries.text: The official vote-counting systems are vulnerable to manipulation and are not audited rigorously enough to detect it.
Fraud may have occurred only in a few strategically important districts, so broad system-level reviews can miss the decisive manipulation.

core_evidence_disconfirming.text: Independent international observers reported that the election followed standard procedures and found no evidence of systematic irregularities in vote counting.
Post-election recounts in several contested districts closely matched the original results within normal error margins.

core_evidence_supporting.text: A local activist group said it had heard reports of suspicious vote handling in a handful of polling stations, but it did not publish verified documentation.

core_evidence_ambiguous.text: A grainy viral video is said to show ballot stuffing in one polling station, but it lacks context and has not been independently verified.

auxiliary_evidence.text: A technical report from a cross-party commission says vote-counting systems were certified by multiple independent auditors, though no audit system can eliminate every theoretical vulnerability.
Analyses of close races examined strategic districts in more detail but did not identify anomalies large enough to change the national outcome.

vignettes.core_claim: Climate change is a hoax invented to control ordinary people.

auxiliaries.text: Climate models are too inaccurate and uncertain to justify treating climate change as a real, well-established phenomenon.
Climate claims may reflect local or cyclical patterns being misread as a global long-term problem.

core_evidence_disconfirming.text: Multiple independent lines of evidence, including temperature records, glacier retreat, sea-level rise, and ocean heat content, show a clear long-term warming trend consistent with increasing greenhouse gas concentrations.
A review of attribution studies concludes that recent warming patterns cannot be explained by short-term local fluctuations alone and are best explained by human-caused greenhouse emissions.

core_evidence_supporting.text: A commentator compiled a list of unusually cold weather events and argued they cast doubt on global warming, but did not compare them to long-term climate trends.

core_evidence_ambiguous.text: A talk-show guest claims that climate alarmism mostly benefits governments and corporations, but offers no empirical data on whether warming itself is unreal.

auxiliary_evidence.text: Retrospective evaluations show that many earlier climate-model projections tracked observed warming reasonably well within their published uncertainty bands.
Global analyses comparing many regions over time find that long-term warming patterns do not reduce to isolated local fluctuations or natural short-term cycles.

vignettes.core_claim: Authorities deliberately hide rising crime rates.

auxiliaries.text: Official crime statistics miss many offences because of narrow definitions and underreporting.
Crime may be rising sharply in particular neighbourhoods or offence categories even if national averages look flat.

core_evidence_disconfirming.text: An independent statistical agency reports that rates for major offences have remained stable or declined slightly over the past decade.
Victimisation surveys and police-record analyses broadly agree that there has not been a large national increase in overall crime.

core_evidence_supporting.text: A neighbourhood campaign group says local residents are experiencing more crime than ever, but it does not provide systematic data beyond local testimonies.

core_evidence_ambiguous.text: Several personal stories on local social media describe crimes people say never show up in the official numbers, but there is no clear evidence about reporting or coding practices.

auxiliary_evidence.text: A methodology report explains that national crime estimates combine police data with survey-based victimisation measures to reduce distortions from underreporting.
Regional breakdowns show that some places and offence types fluctuate, but these do not add up to a clear nationwide hidden surge in crime.

vignettes.core_claim: Mainstream news media always distort political events in favour of the government.

auxiliaries.text: Media bias studies miss the subtle framing choices and topic selection that matter most for real political distortion.
Pro-government distortion may appear most strongly during politically sensitive moments, so broad averages can hide it.

core_evidence_disconfirming.text: Comparative content analyses of several major outlets find a mix of positive, neutral, and negative coverage of government actions, with no consistent pattern of systematic pro-government distortion.
A review of political-news coverage across election cycles found that mainstream outlets frequently publish criticism of sitting governments as well as supportive or neutral reporting.

core_evidence_supporting.text: A blogger collected a few headlines that seemed soft on the government, but did not compare them to the outlets' broader reporting.

core_evidence_ambiguous.text: A commentator argues that mainstream outlets often sound too deferential during crises, but does not provide a systematic comparison with non-crisis coverage.

auxiliary_evidence.text: Recent media-bias studies include framing, tone, and topic-selection measures, and still find roughly balanced critical and supportive coverage across major outlets.
Some high-stakes political moments do show temporary shifts in tone, but evidence that these episodes amount to universal pro-government distortion is limited.

vignettes.core_claim: Pandemic restrictions were primarily a strategy for governments to expand their power permanently.

auxiliaries.text: Analyses claiming restrictions were temporary ignore subtle legal changes and emergency powers that quietly remained after the crisis.
Even if many restrictions were lifted, the most important power expansion may have happened in specific legal or surveillance domains that broad reviews understate.

core_evidence_disconfirming.text: A comparative legal analysis shows that most emergency powers and restrictions were time-limited and have since expired or been rolled back in many jurisdictions.
Follow-up civil-liberties reviews conclude that while some areas deserve scrutiny, there has not been a broad permanent expansion of government power in most countries studied.

core_evidence_supporting.text: A commentator points to a few lingering emergency-era rules as evidence that governments wanted permanent control, but does not compare them to the full set of powers that were withdrawn.

core_evidence_ambiguous.text: A media personality argues that governments enjoyed telling people what to do during the pandemic, offering anecdotes but no systematic evidence about enduring legal change.

auxiliary_evidence.text: Detailed follow-up reports document the legal changes that remained after the pandemic and suggest they are narrower and more visible than broad hidden-power theories imply.
Some surveillance and administrative practices expanded during the pandemic, but evidence that these changes amount to the main or primary purpose of restrictions is limited.
